newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA STOCKS CONVERSION SEEN HAVING LITTLE IMPACT.
newsitem.headline: INDIA STOCKS CONVERSION SEEN HAVING LITTLE IMPACT.

text.p: The government's decision on Tuesday to convert special securities held by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) into marketable securities will not have any immediate impact on the money market, analysts and dealers said.
"There will be no immediate impact on the market," said Aashish Pitale, debt research manager at ICICI Securities and Finance Company.
The government on Tuesday announced it will convert 50 billion rupees of special securities held by the RBI into an equivalent amount of 11.19 percent eight-year bonds.
Special securities are low-interest bearing stocks held by the central bank which are not tradeable.

"Basically what this means is that the RBI has more ammunition for its open market operations," Pitale said. "Earlier it was saddled with illiquid stock at low rates of interest. Now these are converted into paper which can be sold in the market."
Money market dealers said said conversions will not result in any increase in RBI credit to the central government, which have an inflationary impact on the economy.
Dealers said the conversion announced today is the third this year.
Earlier this year, two lots of special securities of 50 billion rupees each were converted into 12.59 percent 2004 and 13.05 percent 2007 bonds.
